quote: Do you see yonder shining light? He said, I think I do. Then said Evangelist, Keep that light in your eye...
meaning: You may not see the goal yet. Keep your eyes on the light.

who: Advayataraka Upanishad 16 · tr. T. R. Srinivasa Ayyangar, 1938
quote: The syllable ‘Gu’ indicates darkness, the syllable ‘Ru’ means its dispeller...
meaning: Gu means darkness. Ru means the one who removes it. That is a guru.

quote: Kabir, I was trailing / The shadows ... / But my Master came / And placed a lamp in my hand.
meaning: I was following shadows. Then my teacher came and gave me a lamp.

who: Hatha Yoga Pradipika 1.3 · tr. Pancham Sinh, 1914
quote: Owing to the darkness arising from the multiplicity of opinions ... Compassionate Swatmarama composes the Hatha Yoga Pradipika like a torch to dispel it.
meaning: Too many opinions make it dark. This book was written as a torch.

who: Chan saying, quoted by Wumen Huikai (1183-1260) · tr. from Chinese
quote: If you want to know the road down the mountain, ask the one who has walked it and come back.
meaning: Want to know the way down? Ask someone who already walked it.

who: Vimalakirti Sutra, ch. 4 · tr. Burton Watson, 1997
quote: ...like a single lamp that lights a hundred or a thousand other lamps, till the darkness is all made bright with a brightness that never ends.
meaning: One light can light many more. Good teaching never runs out.

who: The Buddha, Samyutta Nikaya 45.49 · tr. Bhikkhu Sujato, 2018
quote: Mendicants, the dawn is the forerunner and harbinger of the sunrise. In the same way good friendship is the forerunner and harbinger of the noble eightfold path...
meaning: Dawn comes before the sunrise. A good guide comes before the path.

who: Yoshida Kenko · Essays in Idleness 52, tr. G. B. Sansom, 1911
quote: An old priest prayed at the temples at the foot of a hill, thought that was all, and went home. The shrine was at the top. Kenko: ‘A guide is desirable, even in small matters.’
meaning: Without a guide, he missed the best part. Even small trips need one.

quote: Walk behind the elders and the dog won't bite.
meaning: Follow people who have walked the road before, and you stay safe.

who: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 415, tr. G. U. Pope, 1886
quote: Like staff in hand of him in slippery ground who strays, / Are words from mouth of those who walk in righteous ways.
meaning: Wise people's words are like a walking stick on slippery ground.
